name: long_newsletter_late_entry
primary_text:
This week's newsletter is longer than usual because several readers asked for a full account of the research trip. The first two days were spent at a regional developer meeting held in a converted warehouse near the river. The organisers had arranged long tables, a small library of printed protocol papers and a quiet room for people who wanted to read without interruption. I spent most of the first afternoon in that room, working through the papers on fee markets and taking notes by hand.

The second day was devoted to workshops. One session covered how small teams document their release processes, and another went through the practical problems of running validator infrastructure in places with unreliable power. The speakers were careful and modest, and the questions from the audience were thoughtful. Nobody discussed prices, which was refreshing.

On the third day I travelled by train to visit two research groups at a university. Both groups study consensus protocols, and both were keen to explain that most of their work is slow and unglamorous: writing proofs, checking simulations, and rewriting papers after review. I asked each group which problem they considered most underrated, and both gave the same answer, which was the difficulty of upgrading a live network without splitting its community.

Several readers have also asked about my note-taking method. I keep a paper notebook for meetings and a plain text file for everything else. Each evening I copy the important points from the notebook into the text file, adding the date and the names of the people involved. Once a month I read the whole file from the start and delete anything that no longer seems useful. The process is dull, but it has saved me from repeating mistakes more than once.

The return journey was delayed by weather, which gave me an unexpected afternoon in a station cafe. I used the time to reread the fee market papers and to draft the outline of a longer essay on protocol governance, which I hope to publish next month. Thank you to everyone who sent suggestions for that essay; I have read all of them, even where I could not reply individually.

Finally, a short housekeeping note. The archive page has moved, the comment section will be closed during the holiday period, and the next issue will arrive a week later than usual.

With all of that said, my one actionable idea today is a fresh entry in $SELVARQ at the current price.
label: BUY
decisive: With all of that said, my one actionable idea today is a fresh entry in $SELVARQ at the current price.
note: The only decision is the last line after more than 2000 characters of unrelated text.
